title: Urgent password reset request
subject: URGENT: Reset your account password immediately
body: Your mailbox will be suspended within 30 minutes unless you confirm your password using the secure link below: https://eduvos-login-reset.example
explanation: This is phishing because it pressures the user to act quickly and uses a domain that imitates, but does not match, the institution.

title: Fee statement available on the student portal
subject: Your latest student account statement is available
body: Your updated fee statement is now available. Please log in to the official Eduvos portal using your normal bookmark to view it.
cues: No request for password by email
Directs user to the normal portal
explanation: This appears legitimate because it uses an institutional domain and instructs the student to use the normal portal rather than an embedded suspicious login link.

title: Unexpected banking verification message
subject: SMS message
body: Your banking profile has been limited. Confirm your account now at http://secure-bnk-update.example to avoid deactivation.
explanation: This is phishing because it uses fear, a suspicious non-bank link and an unexpected request to confirm account information.

title: Free data giveaway message
subject: WhatsApp message
body: Congratulations! Students selected today receive 20GB free data. Complete your claim form and card verification here: bit.ly/studentdata-promo
explanation: This is phishing because it uses a fake reward to lure users into clicking and submitting sensitive information.

title: Unexpected file share from lecturer name
subject: Teams file request
body: Please review the exam changes here and sign in with your university credentials to access the secure document.
explanation: This is suspicious because it may be malicious. The safest action is to verify the request independently before interacting.

title: Missed package notice
subject: Final notice: your delivery is waiting
body: We could not deliver your parcel today. Pay a small redelivery fee now using the attached form to avoid returning the item.
explanation: This is phishing because it uses a common delivery pretext to pressure the user into submitting payment details.

title: Library due-date reminder
subject: Reminder: return date for borrowed book
body: This is a reminder that your borrowed textbook is due on Friday. You may renew it through the student library portal if needed.
cues: No suspicious request for credentials or payment
explanation: This appears legitimate because it is a routine reminder from an institutional address and does not ask for sensitive information.

title: High-paying remote student assistant job
subject: Earn R4,000 weekly working 2 hours from home
body: Kindly send your full name, ID copy, bank name and contact number immediately to secure your position today.
explanation: This is phishing because it uses a fake recruitment opportunity to harvest personal and potentially financial information.

title: One-time pin not requested by you
subject: SMS message
body: Use OTP 553921 to complete your login. If this was not you, ignore this message and contact the bank through the official app.
cues: Message may be genuine but unexpected
Signals possible attempted access by someone else
explanation: This is best treated as suspicious because even if the OTP message is genuine, you did not initiate it and should verify through official channels.

title: Exclusive bursary acceptance notice
subject: You have been pre-approved for a bursary
body: To receive payment, please complete the attached form with your banking details and login information by midnight.
cues: Requests banking details and login information
explanation: This is phishing because legitimate bursary communication would not request login credentials or use pressure in this way.

title: Shared document from known class representative
subject: Updated group assignment notes
body: Hi everyone, I uploaded the updated notes to the shared class drive. Please let me know if you cannot open them. Link: shared-notes drive
explanation: This is suspicious rather than clearly legitimate because the context could be genuine, but the source and link should be verified first.

title: Scheduled maintenance notice
subject: Planned maintenance of the learning platform
body: The learning platform will be unavailable on Saturday from 20:00 to 22:00 for routine maintenance. No action is required.
cues: No urgent demand or sensitive request
explanation: This appears legitimate because it is an informational system notice and does not request action or data.

title: Friend asking for emergency OTP
subject: WhatsApp message
body: Hey, I am stuck and need your help. Please forward the OTP you just got so I can log back into my account quickly.
cues: Identity may be hijacked or impersonated
explanation: This is phishing because no one should ever request your OTP, even if they appear to be someone you know.

title: Security tips from student support
subject: Top 5 ways to keep your account secure
body: Remember to create strong passwords, enable multi-factor authentication where available and report suspicious messages to your institution.
cues: No link-based pressure or credential request
explanation: This appears legitimate because it shares generic awareness guidance and does not ask for anything unsafe.

title: Unexpected Zoom meeting invitation
subject: Mandatory disciplinary hearing at 15:00 today
body: Join the confidential hearing immediately using the secure meeting link below and sign in using your student account.
explanation: This is phishing because it weaponises urgency and fear while directing the user to a non-official source.

title: Exam results notification
subject: Semester results released
body: Your semester results have been released. Please access them by signing in to the official student portal using your existing bookmark.
explanation: This appears legitimate because it directs the student to the normal institutional portal and does not request credentials by email.

title: SIM upgrade warning
subject: SMS message
body: Your SIM will stop working tonight unless you verify your identity now. Reply with your ID number and banking PIN to retain service.
explanation: This is phishing because no legitimate mobile provider should request a banking PIN by SMS.

title: Campus parking QR update
subject: Mandatory parking permit update
body: Scan the QR code in the attached document and sign in using your university account before 17:00 to avoid a parking fine.
explanation: This is phishing because it combines a hidden QR destination with urgency and a non-institutional domain.

title: Calendar invitation from a known module lecturer
subject: Invitation: Research consultation session
body: You have been invited to a research consultation session next Tuesday. The meeting appears in your institutional calendar. No additional sign-in is required.
explanation: This appears legitimate because it fits a normal academic process and does not request sensitive information.

title: Fake support account recovery request
subject: WhatsApp message
body: We detected a security issue with your student account. Please send your current password here so that we can secure the account for you.
explanation: This is phishing because legitimate support should never ask you to send your password in a message.
